g.text: Inside an HBM stack: HBM3E vs HBM4 (schematic, not to scale)

text.tspan: SILICON INTERPOSER or CoWoS-L SILICON BRIDGE
stack and GPU sit ~1-2 mm apart, joined by thousands of short, fine wires per stack
a DIMM slot on a motherboard cannot carry 1,024-2,048 parallel wires: HBM must be co-packaged
GPU COMPUTE DIE · HBM PHYs and memory controllers line the die edge
B200/B300: 8 stacks × ~1 TB/s = 8 TB/s · Rubin: 8 stacks × ~2.4 TB/s = 19.2 TB/s
~3× the wafer area per GB of DDR5 (Micron, for HBM3E) · one bad die among 12-16 scraps the whole stack
every die is tested before stacking (known-good die) · heat must cross 12-16 bonded layers
heat must escape up through every layer
thinned wafers, each pierced by thousands
made in the DRAM maker's own process
taller stacks press the package height limit
roughly twice the TSV and bump count
to feed twice the data wires
BASE DIE moves to a LOGIC process
(e.g. TSMC 12 nm; 3 nm-class for custom HBM4E)
PHY + controller logic · 2,048 data wires (32 channels)
from HBM4E: optional CUSTOM base die with buyer's logic
~9.4 Gb/s per pin (Rubin, revised spec) × 2,048 wires

g.text: short reach = low energy per bit
